title: Expose a buried pipe with a bimanual spade and collect the spoil
instruction: Grip the spade's D-handle with the left hand and shaft with the right. Repeatedly slide the blade beneath shallow layers of backfill, lift the load, and dump it into the green spoil tray. Expose at least 80 mm of continuous pipe crown between the two marks and collect at least 120 g of spoil in at least three loaded trips. Keep both grips during work; do not manipulate soil in the bed directly with the robot. Spill no more than 30 g. Finish with the blade clear of the fixture and no more than 5 g left on it. Spade contact with the fixed pipe is allowed.
context: Construction laborers, pipelayers and plumbing helpers excavate and remove backfill with hand tools; landscaping work also includes digging and sprinkler installation. This fixture isolates localized pipe exposure after bulk excavation, relevant to pipe and irrigation maintenance: two-handed tool control, repeated spoil transport and exposure of a buried pipe.
setup: Two YAM arms at the station table. A fixed 300 x 140 mm internal soil fixture is rotated -37 degrees, with centre (0.525, -0.185) m; its side/back walls are 80 mm high and its access lip is 45 mm high. A fixed 33.4 mm diameter, 340 mm long white pipe runs along its length, with axis 30.7 mm above the table. Yellow rim marks bound trench coordinates -20 to +100 mm. Dry loose fill uses the saved soil_shallow_start.npz layout of 3,655 angular convex grains, 8-11 mm across, with total mass 2.669 kg. A 0.45 kg procedural spade with a 125 x 105 mm cupped blade and flat grip sleeves starts on two supports. A fixed green 260 x 240 mm spoil tray has 25 mm rims. Code and saved initial poses specify the complete layout. The reduced fill reaches at most 70 mm above the table before reset settling, about 23 mm above the pipe crown. A thick collider below the room floor catches spilled grains.
scoring: End-state score: 0.25 requires 20 mm contiguous exposed crown, 30 g delivered by spade and one loaded trip; 0.5 requires 40 mm, 70 g and two trips; 1.0 requires 80 mm, 120 g and three trips. Each trip must leave at least 20 g on the tray. Exposure covers the central 16 mm of the pipe crown. More than 30 g spilled, including material below the table, gives zero. Robot contact with soil inside the fixture below its rim, invalid particle state, or spade use without two physically contacting grips for over 0.20 s latches zero for the episode. Material already on the tray or merely swept aside earns no delivery credit. Delivered grains must be off the blade and settled below 20 mm/s for at least 0.25 s. Full success also requires the blade footprint clear of the fixture for an unobstructed final view and no more than 5 g remaining on the blade, with all full-score conditions held for 1 s. Spade-pipe contact is allowed and logged diagnostically; the pipe remains a physical collider.
reset_notes: Restore every grain's saved position and orientation, zero velocities, restore the free spade to its supports, and return the arms to READY. Use object_jitter=0 for the fixed-layout scripted demo. No material is deleted or repositioned during an episode.
fidelity: A scaled test fixture for dry, loose backfill, not a calibrated model of field soil. Angular grains have physical collision, friction, gravity and mass; the spade is held only by finger contact. There is no cohesion, moisture, compaction/fracture model or pipe damage model. Pipe contact is allowed, measured at physics substeps and logged, but not graded as damage or failure. See DESIGN.md for unresolved soil-fidelity and novelty requirements.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,500 steps at 20 Hz, 0 mm exposed, 0 g delivered); demo: 1.0 (1,677 steps at 20 Hz, 105 mm exposed, 273.7 g delivered in 3 loaded trips, 7.7 g spilled)
